task.description: Rework: correct §4's fabricated 'archive/1 has several OTHER callers/contexts' justification per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-02b FAIL verdict, without changing anything else in the design.

result.summary:
Independently re-ran `grep -rn "EventStore.archive(" lib/ test/` before touching the doc. Confirms CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's finding exactly: EventStore.archive/1's ONLY production call site in lib/ is lib/letflow/scheduler.ex:565 (run_retention_sweep/1 itself). All other call sites are direct unit-test invocations: 8 occurrences in test/letflow/event_store_test.exs (lines 693, 777, 783, 817, 849, 869, 1053, 1087) and 1 in test/letflow/engine/reconstruction_test.exs:353. No other production caller exists anywhere in lib/.

Replaced §4's rescue-placement justification sentence (previously: 'archive/1 is a general-purpose context function with several OTHER callers/contexts implied by its own moduledoc ... widening ITS rescue behavior is a larger, less-scoped change than run_retention_sweep/1 ... catching the same narrow error at its own call site'). The new text: (1) states the re-verified grep fact plainly -- one production caller (run_retention_sweep/1 itself), ~10 unit-test call sites, no other production callers exist today; (2) reframes the actual justification around CONTRACT ownership rather than caller count -- archive/1 is EventStore's general-purpose primitive by design intent (moduledoc documents retention-policy precedence and idempotency as reusable properties for whatever calls it, now or later), and its own unit tests deliberately exercise it in isolation and may want a raise on a genuinely-missing schema to propagate (to catch a real bug) rather than be silently folded into {:error, {:schema_unavailable, _}}; widening archive/1's rescue behavior would need checking against every one of those ~10 existing assertions for a behavioral change outside this fix's scope; (3) ties the placement back to §1's own idiom -- rescue at the outermost function whose contract promises graceful degradation (run_retention_sweep/1, the function this design is actually repairing), not inside the shared lower-level primitive it delegates to. The underlying placement decision (rescue in run_retention_sweep/1, not archive/1) is unchanged -- only the stated reason is corrected. No other section of the design doc was touched.
result.routing: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step 2c) to re-check only the corrected §4 justification sentence against the grep evidence above; all other checks already passed in step-02b and require no re-verification per that verdict's own routing.
